4 اقرس العُوُد The branch, or twig, had its sap congealed in it. In the M, instead of جَمَسَ مَاؤُهُ فِيهِ, we find حَبَسَ فِيهِ مَاؤُهُ [which is probably a mistake of a copyist]. (TA.) ＝
-A2- اقرسهُ البَرْدُ [The cold] made him cold; as also ↓ قرّسهُ , inf. n. تَقْرِيسٌ: (S, K:) [or,] accord. to some, by البرد is here meant sleep: (TA:) or the cold made him unable to work with his hand: (JK:) and اقرس البَرْدُ أَصَابِعَهُ the cold made his fingers rigid, by chilness of the extremities, so that he was unable to work. (A, L.) ―
-b2- اقرس المَآءَ فِى الشَّنِّ He cooled the water in the old worn-out skin; (A'Obeyd, TA.) as also قيه ↓ قرّسهُ ; (A'Obeyd, S, A;) and ↓ قَرَسَهُ فبه, inf. n. قَرْسٌ. (A'Obeyd, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
